title: btatt: Enable the detection of ATT transaction timeouts
description:
ATT transaction timeouts (e.g. an ATT request without a response for 30s) are a common failure mode on GATT connections, so being able to detect them would be quite useful. The hard part needed from Wireshark is to scan all the ATT transactions across several bearers potentially and highlight the ones that are incomplete.

Such detection is basically a specialisation of the general problem of matching requests/indications to their responses/confirmations ("Request in Frame" / "Response in Frame"). Looking at the ATT dissector history, I think this used to work at some point but got broken several years back. This has now been fixed under this ticket. An expert info item has been added to indicate incomplete ATT transactions to the user.

Additionally, to avoid ambiguity when the local Host has concurrent GATT connections to multiple remote devices, the ACL connection handle is now used as an extra key to qualify the CID in transaction tracking.

-----

So, this is what exists before the proposed change -- the selected Write Request doesn't indicate the frame where its response can be found:

![image](/uploads/04e7a7b30ee2a34cd48118bc8602a817/image.png){width=900 height=298}

After the proposed changes, the request and its response are now linked in both directions:

![image](/uploads/250c018590899475fe2946c7e1ce5c8e/image.png){width=900 height=312}

This is the new expert-info item indicating a (different) request with a missing response:

![image](/uploads/0e704f260f436684e3db097c8d2a8195/image.png){width=900 height=254}

Users may filter for such packets with `btatt.incomplete_transaction`. It will be up to the user to use other context to determine if an incomplete transaction is really an ATT timeout (e.g. checking if the ATT bearer was disconnected ~30s after the start of the transaction) or can be safely ignored for other reasons (e.g. a clipped HCI trace).

Here's the sample capture:[att_timeout_mini.snoop](/uploads/06d97d236630c65a0f0bbcb8740cb871/att_timeout_mini.snoop)

commits_data.title: btatt: Enable the detection of ATT transaction timeouts
commits_data.message:
btatt: Enable the detection of ATT transaction timeouts

This basically fixes / enhances the transaction tracking so that
requests/indications point to responses/confirmations and vice-versa.

An expert info item is attached to a packet if no response/confirmation
has been observed for that packet so far, so that users may filter for
`btatt.incomplete_transaction` to identify possible ATT timeouts.

commits_data.title: btatt: ATT transaction tracking should account for connection handles
commits_data.message:
btatt: ATT transaction tracking should account for connection handles

The core specification allows the use of separate CID number-spaces
for each logical link (ACL-U, LE-U). Therefore, to correctly track ATT bearer CIDs,
each CID must be qualified by the connection handle of the logical link
that carries that bearer.

This ensures that transactions between the Host and multiple separate
remote devices do not get conflated with each other during dissection.
The same goes for transactions between the Host and the same remote device
but on separate logical links (e.g. GATT over LE vs GATT over BR/EDR).
